title: Introduction: Why Bigger Models Aren't Always Better
text: Hey, I'm Muskin. When people need AI, they reach for the biggest model they can find. But small language models, SLM, are quietly winning a lot of real jobs. So, let's figure out the actual question. When is smaller the smarter choice? First, what an SLM even is. It's a language model, same basic idea as the big ones, but far smaller. text: Giant while being faster, cheaper, and private. Take one real job, routing support tickets to the right team. You don't need a model that can also write poetry and debug code. text: Trap in reverse. For open-ended reasoning, broad world knowledge, or a novel one-off problem, the big model still wins. That's what the extra size buys. So, the rule, reach for a small model when the task is narrow, repeated, and sensitive to cost, speed, or privacy. Reach for a big one when it's open-ended, or you only need it once. title: The Decision Framework: When to Choose SLM vs Frontier LLM
text: Cheaper, private, and just as good. Match the model to the task. Your turn. Pick one AI task you run over and over, classifying, tagging, routing, extracting. Ask, "Does this really need a frontier model or just a small one fine-tuned on my data?" Estimate what you'd save on cost and latency. That's usually where a small model earns its place.
